definition: Logistic Regression is a core concept in Data Science. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Logistic Regression is
theory.body: Logistic Regression describes the methods and patterns used within Data Science to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Logistic Regression is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Logistic Regression matters
theory.body: Without Logistic Regression, systems built with Data Science are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Logistic Regression works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Logistic Regression follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Logistic Regression.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Logistic Regression
theory.body: Logistic Regression offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
